title: Make it respond
summary: Operate a small machine, notice its rule, and predict what it will do next.

scenario.briefing: The campus print shop has an old stamp press. Nobody left instructions. Your job is to work out what it does by trying it, then predict a result you have not seen.

objectives.description: Run the press with more than one input.
Predict an unseen output from the observed rule.
Identify input, processing, and output in a new machine.

hints: Change the number, run the press, and count the marks that appear.
Look for a relationship between the number you enter and the number of marks.
The press prints one mark for each pulse. Try a pulse count of four in your head.
Set the dial to four and press run. You should see four marks. The machine does not add hidden extras.

misconceptions.description: Counting the existing marks instead of the input value.
misconceptions.feedback: The press does not remember the previous run. Reset the press, set the dial, and count only the new marks.

misconceptions.description: Treating a sensor or button as the processing step.
misconceptions.feedback: The sensor produces information. Processing is the decision or calculation made from that information.

sections.title: Every program has three parts
sections.body: A machine receives input, performs processing, and produces output. The stamp press receives the dial value as input, applies a rule, and prints marks as output. The rule is the processing. Programs are precise descriptions of processing.

sections.title: A rule you can predict
sections.body: Once you observe a reliable relationship between input and output, you can predict new cases. Prediction is stronger evidence of understanding than clicking through a demo, because it tests the rule in your head rather than the machine's behavior.

vocabulary.definition: The rule or calculation applied to input.
The visible or stored result of processing.

steps.title: The unlabeled stamp press
steps.prompt: Set the pulse dial and run the press at least twice. Then answer both questions.

prediction.prompt: You reset the press and set the pulse dial to 4. How many marks will appear?
prediction.explanation: The press prints exactly one mark for each pulse, so four pulses produce four marks.

transfer.prompt: A different machine takes the text campus and uppercases every letter. What is its output?
transfer.explanation: The rule is uppercase every letter. The input is lowercase campus, so the output is CAMPUS.

hints: Try pulse values 1, 2, and 3. Watch what changes.
Compare the number on the dial with the number of marks.
The number of marks equals the dial value. Now apply that rule to four.
Reset, choose four, and run. The output is four marks; the transfer machine changes letter case instead of printing.

steps.title: Name the three parts
steps.prompt: Read the explanation, then check your understanding with a new machine.
hints: Input is what goes in. Output is what comes out.
Processing is the decision or calculation in between.
A sensor detects. A controller decides. A light shows.
The sensor supplies input, the controller performs processing, and the light produces output.

sections.title: Input, processing, output
sections.body: Input is information the system receives. Processing is what the system does with it. Output is the result. The same idea appears in a search box, a traffic light, and a calculator.

sections.title: Inputs can be hidden
sections.body: A motion sensor is an input device even though a person does not type anything. A clock, a temperature reading, or a file can also be input. Do not confuse who or what supplies the input with the processing that follows.

vocabulary.definition: A physical component that supplies or displays information.
The part that applies a rule to input and decides an output.

steps.title: Which part processes?
steps.prompt: A motion sensor detects a person. A controller decides the room is now occupied and switches on a light. Which part performs the processing?

options.label: The controller deciding the room is occupied

quiz.explanation: The sensor supplies input, the controller applies a rule, and the light is output.

hints: Which part receives information from the world?
The controller turns a detection into a decision.
Processing is the controller's decision. The sensor is input and the light is output.

accessibility.summary: The machine can be operated with a number field and buttons. All results are also announced as text.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Use Tab to reach the dial, Enter or Space to run, and arrow keys to change number values.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: The printed marks are announced as a count and described as output. The prediction options are ordinary radio buttons.
